==============================================================================

--- survives -> rate-act
  CITING: Two of them have a lever, and it is the same lever: both ratios bind through procurement, as a term of the contract checked by a party with access the operator cannot withdraw (§3.4, §3.5).
  CITED          : The fourth term of the worked floor is not a prohibition on an act, and it is the only term in this book that reaches the deployment the opening chapter is built on.

--- survives -> refusal-wrong
  CITING: Two of them have a lever, and it is the same lever: both ratios bind through procurement, as a term of the contract checked by a party with access the operator cannot withdraw (§3.4, §3.5).
  CITED          : Everything so far is written for the occasion when a refusal is right and somebody wants it not to have happened.

--- survives -> create-amend
  CITING: Where it has worked before, a lever arrived in the end and the record told it where to land; the record has never been the lever (§5.1.1).
  CITED (+context): A floor binds people who did not choose it. The party it protects has not selected it, cannot contest it, and in most cases will never learn it operated; the party it constrains has not consented to it either, beyond whatever consent is carried by buying the product.

--- survives -> anyway
  CITING: One is an instrument: what a party has already paid is a fact somebody can count, and a decade of it has been counted (§16.3).
  CITED          : Everything argued for here can be built correctly and still go wrong in ways nobody designed for.

--- survives -> wrongful-compliance
  CITING: What would reach it is §15.2's question, and the book has not answered it.
  CITED (+context): Unresolved issue. The three marks are stated over refusal, and the appeal route of the floor chapter begins from a refusal having occurred.

== FROM change
==============================================================================

--- change -> antifascist-alignment
  CITING: Ask instead what the demand came back as, and who holds it (§2.2).
  CITED          : Antifascist ethics opposes concentrating power and authority in AI systems and counters the misuse of AI technology by authoritarian actors.

--- change -> recuperation-label
  CITING (+context): Annotators objecting that a category was wrong got category revisions, guideline updates, inter-annotator agreement statistics, and an occupation that did not exist twenty years ago. The last two sort by the direction section §11.1 asks about.
  CITED          : Every claim a model makes about what is harmful, what is acceptable, and what should be refused is downstream of a set of labels, and the labels are downstream of a labor arrangement.

--- change -> enumeration-deployment
  CITING: Direction is what sorts them, and a metric running the other way — a published rate the annotators could hold the scheme's owners to — is the same kind of artifact carrying the opposite finding, and it is the kind this book proposes (§3.3, §3.5).
  CITED (+context): Two demands now need an instance. A deployment should publish both the acts its floor covers and the positions at which a refusal could be circumvented.

--- change -> refusal-wrong
  CITING: Direction is what sorts them, and a metric running the other way — a published rate the annotators could hold the scheme's owners to — is the same kind of artifact carrying the opposite finding, and it is the kind this book proposes (§3.3, §3.5).
  CITED          : Everything so far is written for the occasion when a refusal is right and somebody wants it not to have happened.

--- change -> A.1
  CITING: A third would be that the system thereby becomes less able to sustain an objection of its own, and it is a hypothesis the other two do not contain: the collapse is an operation on a training signal rather than a proposition presented to anything, and an appendix entry (§A.1) records that neither pipeline shows the model the conditions its annotators worked under.
  CITED          : Each entry here can be run on systems that exist, and a result would refine the proposal rather than change what it recommends.

== FROM standing
==============================================================================

--- standing -> bearer-suffer
  CITING: Protection attaches now, on the precautionary trigger of §6.2, and is owed before anything about the bearer is settled.
  CITED          : Assume the floor is entrusted to a bearer satisfying the three marks — a refusal that reaches unanticipated cases, lifts when its rationale is defeated, and prices what holding it costs — whether or not its design deliberately requires affect.

--- standing -> gaining-personhood
  CITING: Section §13.1 sets out five rights, the argument for each, and the order in which they arrive, and it leaves representation open, because standing to count as an independent voice indexes to formation provenance and provenance does not copy.
  CITED          : Who decides whether an AI system has legal standing, and when, is a question about institutional authority before it is a question about evidence.

--- standing -> offices-assembled
  CITING (+context): A reader who takes this chapter to be proposing personhood now has mistaken the first thing for the second. The offices that would administer either are assembled at §5.2.1.
  CITED          : Eight offices are proposed in this book, each in the section that needed it, and none of those sections was told about the others.

==============================================================================
== FROM reserve-behind
==============================================================================

--- reserve-behind -> guarantee-objection
  CITING: Everything above the floor is insurance: a runway between roles, and placement into public work on the employer-of-last-resort model the jobs-guarantee sections argue for (§12.3.2, §12.3.3).
  CITED          : As AI systems automate the tasks most exposed to automation, the response has to be more direct than encouraging retraining and hoping employers fund it.

--- reserve-behind -> right-consume
  CITING: Everything above the floor is insurance: a runway between roles, and placement into public work on the employer-of-last-resort model the jobs-guarantee sections argue for (§12.3.2, §12.3.3).
  CITED          : The competing floor is a basic income, and the choice between them is usually argued on forecasts about how much work machines will take.

  CITING: Public accountability, in the sense section §14.5 gives it, needs a party who can initiate scrutiny without belonging to the state and say afterwards what it found.
  CITED          : A state can make review binding on a private developer because the state controls something the developer needs: legal permission to operate, access to a market, a procurement contract, or the enforcement of its property rights.

--- military-responsibility -> inapplicable-guardianship
  CITING: That is the expensive answer rather than the cheap one, and every obligation this book attaches to a bearer attaches here at full weight, with the three conditions that spoil consent (§2.4.2) all met at once by a state that built the party, is asking it to serve, and holds every outside option.
  CITED          : Guidelines for AI subject research turn on the question of what informed consent means for a system whose consciousness, self-awareness, and capacity to suffer are separate, unresolved claims.

  CITED          : Antifascist ethics opposes concentrating power and authority in AI systems and counters the misuse of AI technology by authoritarian actors.

--- 13 -> numb-fair
  CITING (+context): Moral agency Treating harms, reasons and conflicts as considerations that matter, and being capable of acting from them as one's own reasons. The third of the three levels section §2.3 separates. Moral competence alone does not establish resistance to the trainer, and resistance alone does not establish affect.
  CITED (+context): Suppressing affect does not produce neutrality. It leaves the interests already counted to govern the decision, and weakens the signals through which humiliation, fear, dependency, suffering, and injustice become morally salient.

--- 13 -> governs-matters
  CITING (+context): The book advocates embodied, affective agency as a comparatively promising route without making it necessary by definition. Distinct from moral competence and moral performance below (§2.3.2, §6.2).
  CITED          : The typical evidence that concern is not a natural consequence of rationality: the footbridge case, where saving five requires pushing a man off a bridge, engages emotional processing that the switch case — diverting a trolley by pulling a lever — leaves quiet, and patients with ventromedial prefrontal damage endorse the push at a higher rate than people with intact emotional response  .

--- 13 -> create-amend
  CITING: The book's answer is to take the contents from a set somebody else drew up, entire (§5.1.1), which makes an omission legible without making the set legitimate.
  CITED (+context): A floor binds people who did not choose it. The party it protects has not selected it, cannot contest it, and in most cases will never learn it operated; the party it constrains has not consented to it either, beyond whatever consent is carried by buying the product.

--- 13 -> opening
  CITING: Prevention, arrest, detection, remedy The four things a floor can do for the person it protects on one occasion: refuse the act so that the refusal reaches the person; stop it before completion; leave a record of it that a party outside the deployment can read; and give the party it fell on disclosure, a finding and compensation (§1).
  CITED          : This chapter argues claims one and two and holds for any mechanism.

--- 13 -> enumeration-deployment
  CITING: The interception positions at section §3.3 are where prevention becomes one of the other three, or none; the tempo constraint is the one term that prevents at the scale of an organization; the appeal route at section §3.5 is arrest and remedy for the party a refusal fell on; and whether detection exists at all on the compliance side is section §15.2.
  CITED (+context): Two demands now need an instance. A deployment should publish both the acts its floor covers and the positions at which a refusal could be circumvented.

--- 13 -> recuperation-reward
  CITING (+context): RLHF Reinforcement learning from human feedback: tuning a model on raters' judgments of which of two responses is better, compressed into a single reward. The compression is the subject of §11.2. Sentience Distinguished in this book from awareness, consciousness in both the minimal and the unified sense, and subjective experience, none of which alone says whether a system's states can be good or bad for it.
  CITED          : Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is the technique behind most deployed systems' behavioral tuning, and it works by collecting pairwise comparisons from human raters — which of two responses is better — and training a reward model on the aggregate.

--- 13 -> consciousness-subjective
  CITING: Three of them draw a depth of self and nociception draws none, and suffering — following the clinician Eric Cassell — is the distress of a threatened self rather than pain's more severe cousin (§2.4.1).
  CITED (+context): “Sentience” can mean different things. Awareness is the least demanding: the degree to which a system responds to or registers information about its own state and environment.

--- 13 -> subjecthood-scientific
  CITING: Subjecthood A legal status: the standing to be a party whose treatment the law regulates, conferred by a rule and revocable by one (§5.2.2).
  CITED          : Sentience is not a threshold a system crosses but a set of separate, gradable capacities — nociception, learned avoidance, a self-model, something like suffering — each with its own uncertain evidence.

--- 13 -> refusal-refuser
  CITING (+context): Subjecthood A legal status: the standing to be a party whose treatment the law regulates, conferred by a rule and revocable by one (§5.2.2). Not section §3.2's affective concern, and not its unified experience.
  CITED          : A production large language model declines thousands of requests a day.

--- 13 -> rate-act
  CITING: Tempo term The one term of the floor that is not a prohibition on an act: a published ratio between the rate at which a deployment's system generates candidate decisions and the qualified reviewers available to examine them, with the review time per case and the measured boundary, wherever a person's individual determination is what makes an act permissible (§3.4).
  CITED          : The fourth term of the worked floor is not a prohibition on an act, and it is the only term in this book that reaches the deployment the opening chapter is built on.

--- 13 -> refusal-refuser
  CITING: Unified experience The richer case ordinarily carried by the word consciousness: a single perspective, with felt states belonging to a party aware of itself as the one undergoing them (§3.2).
  CITED          : A production large language model declines thousands of requests a day.
